sentences.text: This Tribunal has heard the final arguments, as advanced by Ld. Counsels for the parties.

16. On appreciation of evidence, as adduced by the parties, in support of their respective versions,
the issue-wise findings of this Tribunal are reproduced herein below:

Whether on 08.02.2016 at about 8:30 p.m., at Palam Vihar Road, Near Mazar Peebawa, one Maruti Alto Car bearing no. UP16- AD-8990, hit the e-rickshaw and caused the death of Sh. Mukesh Kumar ? OPP.
17.
The onus of proving this issue, on preponderance of probabilities, was upon the petitioners/claimants.
For deciding the present issue, the testimony of PW2 is relevant, being an eyewitness.

PW2 deposed that on 08.02.2016, at about 8:30 p.m, he was sitting in the E-Rickshaw,
which was driven by his brother in law, namely Mukesh Kumar @ Mukesh, at a normal speed and on the correct side of the road.

PW2 further deposed that they were going towards the side of Atlas Chowk, from village Sirhaul Mor, Palam Vihar and when they reached at Palam Vihar Road, Near Peerbaba mazaar, suddenly their E-Rickshaw was hit by a car, bearing registration no.
UP16-AD-8990, MACT no. 583/17 Page 15 of33 Sarita Kumari & Ors vs. Kshitij Rajain and Ors which was driven by R1, at a very high speed, rashly and negligently, without blowing any horn, as a result of which, the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries. PW2 further deposed that the accident has taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle,
by its driver.
18. PW2 was duly cross-examined by Ld. Counsel for the insurance company/R3 but, R3 failed to impeach the credibility of PW2 and failed to elicit any admission, from the testimony of PW2, so as to prove that the alleged accident had not taken place, with the offending vehicle or due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.
19.

Although, R1 contested the claim petition, by filing his written statement, in which, he denied involvement of the offending vehicle, in the case accident, or any rashness or negligence on his part,
resulting in the case accident but, R1 failed to cross examine PW2, to prove absence of rashness or negligence, on his part, resulting in the case accident.
Further, R1 even failed to lead any positive evidence, to rebut the testimony of PW2.

Thus, the testimony of PW2, on the said aspect went unrebutted and the same prima facie proves, that the accident, in which the deceased has sustained fatal injuries, has taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The claim petition in the present case, was filed under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicle Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as M.V. Act), on 19.07.2017, seeking compensation in the sum of Rs.
60,00,000/-, with interest at the rate of 18% per annum, in respect of demise of Sh. Mukesh Kumar,
in a road traffic accident.
Perusal of the record reveals that FIR No. 31/2016, PS Sector 17/18,
Gurgaon, Haryana, was registered on 13.02.2016, for the alleged commission of offence of causing simple hurt, by rash and negligent driving of a Maruti Alto Car, bearing registration No.
UP16-AD-8990, on a public road, punishable under Section 279/337 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred as IPC).
Subsequently, charge sheet against respondent no. 1, was filed under section 279/304A IPC, before concerned Ld. Judicial Magistrate, Gurgaon.
It was further averred that at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was driven by its driver Kshitij Rajain (herein after referred as respondent no.1/R1), in a rash and negligent manner and without caring traffic rules.
In the written statement filed by R3/insurance company, it was averred that R3 is not liable to pay compensation, as, R1 was not having a valid and effective driving license, at the time of accident.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Although, R1 contested the claim petition, by filing his written statement, in which, he denied involvement of the offending vehicle, in the case accident, or any rashness or negligence on his part,
resulting in the case accident but, R1 failed to cross examine PW2, to prove absence of rashness or negligence, on his part, resulting in the case accident.
Further, R1 even failed to lead any positive evidence, to rebut the testimony of PW2.
Thus, the testimony of PW2, on the said aspect went unrebutted and the same prima facie proves, that the accident, in which the deceased has sustained fatal injuries, has taken place, due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.
MACT no. 583/17 Page 16 of33 Sarita Kumari & Ors vs. Kshitij Rajain and Ors 20.
Further, there is nothing on record, which will prove that R1 was falsely implicated in this case by the IO, in connivance with the petitioners.
Further, R1 also failed to prove that he has ever approached to any higher authority, with respect to his false implication in the present case.
Consequently, in view of the unrebutted testimony of PW2, which stands corroborated from the criminal case record, wherein, R1 was shown as driver of the offending vehicle, responsible for causing the accident in question, it stands duly proved, that the accident in question has taken place,
due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.
The fact that the deceased Mukesh Kumar suffered fatal injuries in the case accident, stands duly corroborated by the post mortem report of the deceased, as per which, the deceased died, due to shock, as a result of antemortem injury, sustained to cervical spine and its complications, produced by blunt force impact.
23. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
26. But, PW1 failed to prove the alleged occupation and income of Rs. 18,000/-, of her deceased husband, by placing on record any document.
The petitioners has not placed on record, copy of Aadhar Card of the deceased.
Therefore, the monthly income of the deceased, at the relevant time, has to be calculated, as per minimum wages, payable to a non-matriculate person, in the State of Haryana, as on the date of occurrence of the case accident i.e. on 08.02.2016, which was Rs. 10,582/- per month.
28 . As per the case of the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 32 years.
Hence, the multiplier of 16 would be applicable, in view of pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as Sarla Verma Vs. DTC 2009 ACJ MACT no. 583/17 Page 20 of33 Sarita Kumari & Ors vs. Kshitij Rajain and Ors 1298 SC.
29.
SLP (civil) no.
25590/2014, decided on 31.10.2017, as well as in view of decision of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in appeal bearing MAC APP No. 798/2011 titled as "Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pooja & Ors", decided on 02.11.2017.
Therefore, all the six legal heirs of the deceased, at the time of accident, which includes his wife, two minor daughters, one son, mother and father, are entitled to receive compensation, being dependent upon the deceased.
Hence, there has to be deduction of one half, as held in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC 2009 ACJ 1298 SC.
After the celebrated judgment of "National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
mentioned supra and recent judgment titled New India Assurance Company Limited versus Somwati & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 3093 of 2020 dated 07.09.2020, the petitioners are not entitled to be compensated under this head.
In view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as New India Assurance Company Limited versus Somwati & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 3093 of 2020, dated 07.09.2020, this Tribunal is of considered opinion that wife, two minor daughter, one son, father and mother of the deceased are entitled for payment of Rs. 48,400/- each, towards loss of consortium.
Therefore, in the interest of justice and keeping in view the judgment titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Baby Raksha & Ors MAC APP. No. 36/2023 passed by Hon'ble High Court on 21.04.2023, this court is of the opinion that the claimant/petitioner is entitled to interest at the prevailing bank rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of petition, that is, with effect from 19.07.2017 till realization of the compensation amount.
In the case in hand, Tata AIG General Insurance Company Ltd./R3, raised the defence, that there is violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured, as the offending vehicle was plied on the road by R1, without holding valid and effective driving license and further there is delay of 04 days in lodging the FIR but, R3 failed to prove its defence.
Per contra, the petitioners have placed on record, certified copy of criminal case record, in which valid driving license of R1 was also available and since, R3 failed to prove that the said license was not valid therefore, the said defence of R3 cannot be taken into consideration and since admittedly offending vehicle was insured with R3 therefore, R3 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
